blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم باب فضل انظارالمعسر... رقم:٤٠٠٠
blocks.tamil_translation: “Whoever wishes that Allah Ta'ala should save him from the hardships of the Day of Qiyamah, let him give time to those suffering in poverty (to a debtor), or forgive (all or part of what is owed to him” — Hazrat Abu Qatadah (RA) narrates that he heard Rasulullah ﷺ say this.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَنَسٍ ﵁ قَالَ: خَدَمْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ عَشْرَ سِنِيْنَ بِالْمَدِيْنَةِ وَاَنَا غُلَامٌ لَيْسَ كُلُّ اَمْرِيْ كَمَا يَشْتَهِيْ صَاحِبِيْ اَنْ يَكُوْنَ عَلَيْهِ، مَاقَالَ لِيْ فِيْهَا اُفٍّ قَطُّ، وَمَا قَالَ لِيْ لِمَ فَعَلْتَ هذَا اَمْ اَلَّا فَعَلْتَ هذَا.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابوداؤد باب في الحلم واخلاق النبي ﷺ رقم:٤٧٧٤
blocks.tamil_translation: “I served the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah for ten years. Since I was young in age, not all of my work was as the Prophet ﷺ wished. Because of my young age many mistakes would happen through me, (but in these ten years) the Prophet ﷺ never even said “Ugh” to me. He never once asked me, “Why did you do this work?” or “Why did you not do this work?””.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ اَنَّ رَجُلاً قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ: اَوْصِنِيْ قَالَ: لَا تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لَا تَغْضَبْ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه البخاري باب الحذر من الغضب رقم:٦١١٦
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates: “A man requested Rasulullah ﷺ, “Give me some advice.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Do not become angry.” The man made the same request again and again, and each time the Prophet ﷺ replied only, “Do not become angry.”
